Content:
In some geometry problems involving triangles, we have to apply a mix of different theorems to find the solution.

Content:
For example, consider the diagram below, where [MATH: l_1 \parallel l_2.] What is the value of [MATH: x?]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/00b7c07094a0af0665a62c7780baf9df]

Content:
Since [MATH: l_1 \parallel l_2], we can draw a line perpendicular to both. Let's draw that line passing through the point [MATH: B,] as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/2c07fe14bfdeedaf3418ac6a51c2cdbf]

Content:
The sum of the measures of the interior angles of a triangle is [MATH: 180^\circ.] Therefore, for [MATH: \triangle BED,] we have
[MATH: 25^{∘} + 90^{∘} + m∠DBE|= 180^{∘}; 115^{∘} + m∠DBE|= 180^{∘}; m∠DBE|= 65^{∘}.]

Content:
Since the straight angle [MATH: \angle CBE] must have a measure of [MATH: 180^\circ,] we have
[MATH: m∠DBE + 45^{∘} + m∠ABC|= 180^{∘}; 65^{∘} + 45^{∘} + m∠ABC|= 180^{∘}; 110^{∘} + m∠ABC|= 180^{∘}; m∠ABC|= 70^{∘}.]

Content:
Finally, in [MATH: \triangle ACB,] we have
[MATH: x + 90^{∘} + m∠ABC|= 180^{∘}; x + 90^{∘} + 70^{∘}|= 180^{∘}; x + 160^{∘}|= 180^{∘}; x|= 20^{∘}.]
